evidence: app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].js:272-275 — reviewer would ask: distinguish 404 from other failures before merging
app/src/routes/404.js:8 — one-line fix: set responseInit.status = 404
app/src/lib/api.js — reviewer would ask to split fetch/caching from formatting/domain indexes

review_cost.rationale: No structural rework needed, but there is a definite round of changes: error-status handling, the api.js split, the not-found dedup, and the 404 status — all small, all things a careful reviewer would request before approving.

findings.issue: The catch block sets responseInit.status = 404 for every failure, so API/network/500 errors render a 'Not found' page with a 404 status; the same pattern is in moves/[name].js:47, abilities/[name].js:45 and types/[name].js:71.
findings.suggestion: Check error.status === 404 for the not-found path; otherwise log and set 500 with a distinct server-error template.

findings.issue: 247-line god module mixing the fetch client, global cache, display formatting, CSS class naming and domain indexes; every route depends on it.
findings.suggestion: Split into api/client.js (fetch + cache), api/pokemon.js (indexes/maps), and lib/format.js (humanize, englishName, dexNumber, displayValue); move typeClassName into components.js.

findings.issue: The catch-all 404 route serves its page with HTTP 200.
findings.suggestion: Use the handler's responseInit parameter to set status 404, as the other routes already do.

findings.issue: The 'Not found' template is duplicated five times across routes (404.js:14, pokemon/[name].js:287, abilities/[name].js:58, moves/[name].js:60, types/[name].js:84).
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared notFoundTemplate() into src/lib/components.js and reuse it from the handlers' notFound branch.

findings.issue: When the refresh fetch fails or returns non-ok, the old results stay on screen while the URL has already been updated — visible state and address bar disagree.
findings.suggestion: On failure, either restore the previous URL/history entry or surface an inline error message; at minimum retry or fall back to a full navigation.

findings.issue: The undocumented GRACILE_BUILD env gate is duplicated in all six route files, and the build output (dist/server/entrypoint.js) shows server-mode builds don't invoke handlers, so it may be entirely dead code.
findings.suggestion: Hoist a single isBuild guard into src/lib/api.js (or verify it's needed and document why in a comment).

findings.issue: Module-level response cache never evicts successful entries; safe only because the API is a fixed snapshot — against the live API the spec describes, memory grows with distinct URLs forever.
findings.suggestion: Cap the Map (simple LRU) or add a TTL, keeping the rejected-promise eviction that already exists.

findings.issue: getRecordByUrl has a dead conditional — both branches return getJson(url).
findings.suggestion: Reduce to a one-liner export, or make the absolute-URL branch meaningful (e.g. rewrite pokeapi.co URLs to the configured API base).

findings.issue: Empty directory committed in the source tree.
findings.suggestion: Delete it (or move components.js here if the features/ convention is intended).

findings.issue: All move table headers render aria-sort="none" initially even though the Level Up table is server-sorted by level, so the initial sort state is misreported to assistive tech.
findings.suggestion: Mark the initially-sorted column (Level for level-up tables, Move otherwise) with aria-sort="ascending" in the server render.

summary: This is a solidly idiomatic Gracile 0.11 app: document/route/client-script conventions, the Express adapter, and the version pin all match the framework's current docs and starters, and correctness fundamentals (escaping, race guards, cache eviction) are handled. The main debt is structural — a god-module api.js, a five-fold duplicated not-found template, and an error handler that conflates every failure with 404 — plus a 200-status catch-all and a silently-stale client refresh. Mergeable after one round of small, mechanical changes; nothing requires rework.
